UGOD 5005.title: Generative AI Methods of 3D Design and Optimization for Adaptive Environments
UGOD 5005.description: This course investigates generative AI techniques for creating and optimizing complex 3D spatial designs for interior and exterior environments. Students will master AI-driven modeling, generative algorithms, and multiobjective optimization to produce designs that balance aesthetic vision with critical real-world constraints. The curriculum focuses on building intelligent design systems, bridging AI creativity with practical implementability in architecture, urban planning, and smart infrastructure.
cilos: Apply Generative AI Models to synthesize complex 3D spatial design for both interior and exterior environments.
Formulate spatial design problems as Multi-Objective Optimization (MOO) challenges, translating design goals into quantifiable, competing performance metrics (e.g., cost, energy, aesthetics).
Integrate and encode practical Real-World Constraints (e.g., building codes, constructability) into the generative design process using computational and algorithmic methods.
Evaluate the performance of AI-generated design solutions using validated computational simulation tools and established metrics for urban and architectural projects.
Communicate the technical process, findings, and viability of the optimized design proposals effectively to both specialist and general audience groups.

UGOD 5009.title: Inferential Statistics and OLS Regression
UGOD 5009.description: This course introduces fundamental knowledge and practice of basic statistics in quantitative social science research, with a focus on how quantitative methods are used to assemble, describe, and draw inferences from bodies of numerical data. The course serves as an additional foundation for more advanced methodology courses (such as UGOD 5020). The course covers two modules. The first is about descriptive statistics and fundamentals of statistical inference. Topics include frequency distribution, probability theory, random variable and probability distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing, t-test, Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), and contingency table analysis. The second is about linear regression techniques, which are widely used in social science research. The course materials are explored through the analyses of real data sets using STATA.

UGOD 5010.title: Science of Cities
UGOD 5010.description: The course aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the city and the system of cities, the challenges faced by cities, especially the rapidly-developing large cities, and the key tools for interventions in response to critical pressures linked to economic development, urbanization, globalization, migration, social inclusion, climate change, resource efficiency, technology etc.
cilos: Demonstrate an understanding of the intellectual history of urban planning and designs.
Analyze selected cities as the cases of planning and designs.
Develop a new notion of cities as systems of networks and flows instead of places in space.
Apply new tools to understand different aspects of city structure.
Compare design and decision-making models that predict interactions and flow in future cities.
Write  Report on Case Study.

UGOD 5011.title: Applied Numerical Methods
UGOD 5011.description: This course introduces computational methods that are commonly used in social science (e.g. economics, finance etc.) and other disciplines (e.g. engineering). They are to solve/handle linear and non-linear equations, optimizations, numerical integration and differentiation, function approximation, dynamic models (discrete and continuous), etc. Classes will be interactive so that students can understand both theory and practice. Homework is designed for students to be familiar with those techniques.
cilos: Be familiar with one scientific programming language proficiently, e.g. Matlab, Julia, etc.
Understand various numerical methods.
Identify proper numerical methods for solving specific problems.
Apply numerical methods to solve problems on computer.
Combine methods learned or design new methods to solve problems in own research using a programming language.

UGOD 5020.title: Quantitative Social Science
UGOD 5020.description: This course builds on the knowledge of the linear regression models to introduce students advanced statistical methods to analyze survey, administrative and other types of data of interest to quantitative social scientists. The introduction of statistical methods is integrated into research contexts and designs from a holistic framework and bridge quantitative social science and computational social science (data science). Topics include measurement, prediction, causal inference, natural experiment and program evaluation (difference-in-differences, panel data, instrumental variables, regression discontinuity), applied to both survey and big data.
cilos: Apply statistical methods when the assumptions of classical linear regression are violated.
Understand the concept of causality and research designs to establish causal relationship.
Utilize some standard methods in causal inferences with observational data.
Apply basic tools to analyze different types of data, including big data.
Perform essential techniques to analyze big social data.
Write a research report on findings.

UGOD 5030.title: GIS and Spatial Analysis
UGOD 5030.description: This course introduces students to the basic concepts and methods in Geographic Information System (GIS), and their applications in urban design and governance, environmental and infrastructure sustainability, and smart city management. This course integrates social science and informatics perspectives, and is suitable for students with various backgrounds. In addition to learning traditional GIS data, spatial analytical techniques, and GIS software, this course also develops skills of manipulating spatially detailed urban sensing Big Data (about urban activities, environmental qualities, and mobility patterns).
cilos: Demonstrate an understanding of  common GIS concepts and spatial data models.
Manipulate tabular and spatial data to produce intelligible graphics.
Apply major extensions and data analysis functions in ArcGIS for problem solving.
Perform basic (satellite) image processing tasks.
Perform basic hot spot and other spatial statistical analysis.
Write report on findings.

UGOD 5040.title: Social Data Acquisition and Analysis
UGOD 5040.description: The course introduces students to a comprehensive understanding of how to leverage various types of data to answer critical questions in the social sciences for urban analysis. We will explore fundamental concepts and methodologies in social and population data collection, including, sampling surveys designs and analysis. Since alternative data sources (e.g., passive measurement, social media and simulated data generated by large language models (LLMs) become increasingly available, the course will explore cutting edge methods for collecting and analyzing data, and how they can be used in combination with traditional survey data.
cilos: Demonstrate an understanding of the basic ideas, concepts and principles of probability sampling from an applied perspective.
Identify and appropriately apply sampling techniques to survey design problems.
Identify the pros and cons for each of data collection methods, the implication of survey design decisions on data quality.
Test new technology on wearables, sensors, and apps, and methods for collecting and analyzing web data.
Perform statistical analysis of complex sample survey data, census data, or other data, and integrated data.
Integrate data from different sources to design a research project.

UGOD 5040.title: Urban Data Acquisition and Analysis
UGOD 5040.description: The course introduces students to different methods of collecting data in the social sciences for urban analysis, focusing on sampling surveys designs and analysis in urban settings. Since alternative data sources (e.g., passive measurement, social media and administrative data) become increasingly available in recent years, the course will also cover other modes of data acquisitions such as using new  technology on wearables, sensors, and apps in urban research settings, and exploration of cutting edge methods for collecting and analyzing web data, and how they can be used in combination with traditional survey data.
cilos: Demonstrate an understanding of the basic ideas, concepts and principles of probability sampling from an applied perspective.
Identify and appropriately apply sampling techniques to survey design problems.
Identify the pros and cons for each of data collection methods, the implication of survey design decisions on data quality.
Test new technology on wearables, sensors, and apps, and methods for collecting and analyzing web data.
Perform statistical analysis of complex sample survey data, census data, or other data, and integrated data.
Integrate data from different sources to design a research project.

UGOD 5050.title: Cities and Society
UGOD 5050.description: The course looks at some of the major drivers of urban inequality and poverty, and the key actions that cities are taking to reduce urban inequalities through urban design, infrastructure and policy. Students are introduced with tools to analyze the socio-demographic profile of households and neighborhoods/communities and their relation to spatial distribution and clustering in cities of both the developing and the developed world. A particular emphasis is placed on identifying spatial strategies that can alleviate the concentration of urban poverty and inequality to enhance urban social cohesion by optimizing access to jobs, housing, education, health, public space, transport and community infrastructure.
cilos: Describe the major issues related to cities and society.
Explain the major drives of urban inequality and poverty issues in different countries.
Apply quantitative approach to analyze the socio-demographic profile of households and neighborhoods in cities.
Identify an urban issue and conduct independent research and present findings.

UGOD 5060.title: Urban Data Analytics
UGOD 5060.description: Over recent years, especially with the rise of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the way data are used to understand urban system has changed dramatically. Cities are constantly adapting to incorporate new technology, and urban social life increasingly occurs in digital environments and continues to be mediated by digital systems, producing urban data not only in volume but also in form (i.e. text, image, audio, and video). This course delves into the challenges and opportunities of using new and emerging forms of data to study cities.
cilos: Describe the opportunities and challenges created by digital big data.
Extract and manage urban big data.
Utilize basic graphic tools to visualize and analyze exemplary big data.
Perform basic text and image processing tasks.
Demonstrate an understanding of the basic knowledge of Agent-based Modeling.
Critically evaluate research that use big data and computational methods.

UGOD 5060.title: Urban Data Analytics
UGOD 5060.description: Over recent years, the way data are used to understand urban system has changed dramatically. Cities are constantly adapting to incorporate new technology, and urban social life increasingly occurs in digital environments and continues to be mediated by digital systems, producing urban data not only in volume but also in form (i.e. text, image, audio, and video). This course delves into the challenges and opportunities of using new and emerging forms of data to study cities.
cilos: Describe the opportunities and challenges created by digital big data.
Extract and manage urban big data.
Utilize basic graphic tools to visualize and analyze exemplary big data.
Perform basic text and image processing tasks.
Demonstrate an understanding of the basic knowledge of Agent-based Modeling.
Critically evaluate research that use big data and computational methods.

UGOD 5066.title: AI Agents for Human Mobility
UGOD 5066.description: This course examines human travel behaviors and mobility patterns across spatial and temporal dimensions, with a strong emphasis on the complex interactions between individual behavior and the urban environment. The course offers an interdisciplinary introduction to building AI-driven agent frameworks to understand, model, and simulate human mobility, and explore how urban environment, socio-economic factors, and other constraints shape individual and collective mobility patterns. Through theoretical frameworks, advanced analytical methods, and empirical tools (e.g., GPS tracking, mobile data), the course decodes how humans adapt their spatio-temporal travel behavior to evolving urban landscapes. Case studies on commuting efficiency, activity scheduling, accessibility disparities, and disaster resilience, and emerging trends such as shared mobility systems and virtual spaces will be covered. Through hands-on modeling and industry-linked case studies, students will learn to build and evaluate AI-agent systems for human mobility and urban studies.
cilos: Be familiar with key behavioral geography theories.
Know where and how to get urban spatio-temporal travel behavior data.
Analyze urban spatiotemporal behavior data.
Design AI agents for urban spatio-temporal mobility in urban scenarios.

UGOD 5070.title: Urban Planning and Design
UGOD 5070.description: This course cuts across all major fields within urban planning and design and introduces the major theories, models, and methodological approaches that urban planners and policy makers use for urban planning and design. This course also critically examines the current practice of urban planning and governance in China at various geographical scales.
cilos: Identify and assess the major theories and methodological approaches of urban planning and design.
Understand descriptive and prescriptive approaches for examining urban form and function.
Have a broad understanding of the major epochs in urban planning and the ways they attempted to shape the design and function of cities.
Evaluate current policy and planning challenges affecting Chinese cities.
Formulate questions in the field of urban planning and design for in-depth exploration.
Use a big data lens to examine planning and design issues and solutions.

UGOD 5080.title: Economic Analysis of Cities and the Environment
UGOD 5080.description: This interdisciplinary course will provide students a systematic framework of the interplay between urban growth and the environment from economic perspectives.By walking them through the state-of-the-art research in urban and environmental economic studies from both developing and developed countries, it will familiarize students with popular empirical strategies in applied economics and relevant fields to solve the most pressing environmental challenges accompanied with fast-urbanized cities. By the end of the class, students will be equipped with toolkits to evaluate policy questions in transportation, pollution and health, climate change, energy transition, housing market, and environmental justice.
cilos: Improve critical, innovative, and independent economic thinking skills.
Compare and contrast the state-of-the-art research in urban and environmental studies.
Learn the econometric approaches commonly used in empirical studies.
Understand and critically assess the urban and environmental challenges especially in China.
Expand their toolkits on urban and environmental policy evaluation.
Effectively conduct oral, written, and visual communication.

UGOD 5080.title: Economic Analysis of Cities and the Environment
UGOD 5080.description: This interdisciplinary course will provide students a systematic framework of the interplay between urban growth and the environment from economic perspectives.By walking them through the state-of-the-art research in urban and environmental economic studies from both developing and developed countries, it will familiarize students with popular empirical strategies in applied economics and relevant fields to solve the most pressing environmental challenges accompanied with fast-urbanized cities. By the end of the class, students will be equipped with toolkits to evaluate policy questions in transportation, pollution and health, climate change, energy transition, housing market, and environmental justice.
cilos: Improve critical, innovative, and independent economic thinking skills.
Compare and contrast the state-of-the-art research in urban and environmental studies.
Learn the econometric approaches commonly used in empirical studies.
Understand and critically assess the urban and environmental challenges especially in China.
Expand their toolkits on urban and environmental policy evaluation.
Effectively conduct oral, written, and visual communication.

UGOD 5090.title: Urban Sustainability
UGOD 5090.description: This course provides a road map for examining the sustainability of cities through perspectives and approaches in urban governance and design. Drawing from an interdisciplinary literature, we will explore the following major themes in the context of urban sustainability: theories and assessment tools of urban sustainability, land use and transportation, urban design, energy and climate change, food and health, governance, and social ecology.
cilos: Understand the debates over what constitutes “urban sustainability” and the complexities in measuring it.
Discuss the current literature on the three components of sustainability from an urban development perspective.
Explore what “actually-existing sustainability” may look like in urban governance and design practice.
Apply assessment tools for each of the components of sustainability for a project, plan, program or policy.
Write a research proposal on urban sustainability.

UGOD 5100.title: Public Finance and Taxation
UGOD 5100.description: Public finance refers to that government uses (tax) policy tools to finance its spending on various areas. It is thus an important aspect of urban governance and public policy. This course introduces some classical results of the taxation theory as well as recent developments on the empirical side of tax policy. The topics include labor income tax, business taxes (such as corporate income tax and dividend tax), savings tax, inheritance tax etc. We also talk about urban (or local) tax policy and its effects on local economy.
cilos: Understand the efficiency cost of taxation.
Identify the benefits and costs of a change in certain tax policy.
Know various types of tax and their role in public finance.
Understand the concept of causality and research designs to establish causal relationship.
Apply statistical or theoretical methods to conduct independent tax policy analysis.
Write a research report on tax policy.

UGOD 5101.title: Empirical Methods for Urban Research
UGOD 5101.description: The course introduces students to basic practices and tools that will enhance their ability to conduct empirical research and analysis in applied economics and relevant disciplines in a data-rich world. By the end of the course, the students will be proficient in a variety of data management, visualization, and quantitative techniques necessary to efficiently conduct independent research. Specifically, students will be able to utilize multiple types of data such as tabular, spatial, image and text data in their own research. The course format is “hands-on”, and students will conduct most of their work on their personal computers using R and RStudio.
cilos: Apply reproducible R programming in the context of urban science and relevant disciplines.
Gather, manipulate, and visualize various types of data effectively for research purposes.
Analyze different types of data.
Employ simulation and resampling methods in applied research.
Conduct independent academic research.
Effectively conduct oral, and visual communication.

UGOD 5101.title: Empirical Methods for Urban Research
UGOD 5101.description: The course introduces students to basic practices and tools that will enhance their ability to conduct empirical research and analysis in applied economics and relevant disciplines in a data-rich world. By the end of the course, the students will be proficient in a variety of data management, visualization, and quantitative techniques necessary to efficiently conduct independent research. The course format is “hands-on”, and students will conduct most of their work on their personal computers using R and RStudio.
cilos: Apply reproducible R programming in the context of urban science and relevant disciplines.
Gather, manipulate, and visualize various types of data effectively for research purposes.
Analyze different types of data.
Employ simulation and resampling methods in applied research.
Conduct independent academic research.
Effectively conduct oral, and visual communication.

UGOD 5102.title: Life Course Research
UGOD 5102.description: Life course analysis provides a framework to understand many topics across different disciplines, such as family and fertility, migration, child development and education, paid and unpaid work, and wellbeing, heath and ageing. Those decisions or outcomes of individuals are a result of how individuals interact with each other in the specific culture and historical context that is shaped by our city, policy, and environment. This course will introduce the field of life course research and basic concepts, cover a range of established research topics, with a focus on the theoretical and substantive research in addition to the translation of these research questions into empirical applications. Another central goal will be the introduction of event history techniques and sequence analysis. Students will learn how social survey data, administrative data, and geographic information are synthesized to answer those research questions.
cilos: Name, define, compare and give concrete form to the central theories, concepts and methodological approaches within life course research.
Name and critically assess the research design, theoretical approach, and methodology of several life course studies.
Identify different types of event history analysis applications and when to apply them.
Explain the application of sequence analysis and when to use them.
Develop a deep understanding in one of the life course research topics with a detailed literature review and critically identify the research gap with proper research design to tackle this gap.
Undertake an event history analysis or sequence analysis using the computer program R and interpret and present the results of this analysis in the form of a research paper.

UGOD 5103.title: Economics of the Urban Labor Market
UGOD 5103.description: This course studies theoretical and empirical issues in economics of the urban labor market. Topics include theories and empirics of human capital in an urban area, labor search and matching, unemployment, and their applications. The modeling and empirical tools covered allow students to analyze various public policy issues facing contemporary urban governance and design, including minimum wage and unemployment benefits. Evidence from China’s urban labor market will be discussed along the course.
cilos: Explain the modern theories of employment and the urban labor market.
Analyze contemporary public policy issues concerning the labor market.
Describe and critically assess the literature on employment and the urban labor market.
Present and communicate recent research on employment and the urban labor market.
Write an original research paper on employment and the urban labor market.

UGOD 5104.title: Visualization for Urban Informatics
UGOD 5104.description: As urban areas continue to grow and become more complex, the amount of data generated by cities has increased exponentially. This presents significant challenges in terms of managing and interpreting urban data to address various urban issues or challenges. In response to this, our course is designed to equip students with the skills needed to visualize urban data, enabling them to gain a better understanding of city structure and dynamics. Moreover, this course will provide students with the knowledge and tools needed to conduct sustainable planning and design towards a sustainable society.

UGOD 5105.title: Urban Complexity Analysis and Modeling
UGOD 5105.description: Going beyond conventional GIS and geospatial analysis, this course delves into the realm of complexity-science methods, including fractal geometry, power law statistics, space syntax, complex networks, scaling hierarchy, and cellular automata. By embracing pivotal concepts like "natural streets" and "natural cities," alongside the tools such as Axwoman and head/tail breaks, students will explore city structure and dynamics from a complexity-science perspective. These concepts, methods and tools will be applied to open-access geospatial big data such as OpenStreetMap, nighttime imagery, and location-based social media data for revealing insights into cities for better transforming modern cities towards a sustainable planet.

UGOD 5110.title: Quantitative Macroeconomics
UGOD 5110.description: This course introduces the framework of modern macroeconomics and then conducts policy analysis based on it. We start from the classic economic growth model developed by Solow, then gradually add other features to the model to make it better explain the real world. These features include a life-cycle structure, income risks, incomplete credit markets, the role of government, etc. After building up the framework, we study its policy implications with a focus on fiscal policy.

UGOD 5112.title: AI Vision for Urban Sensing
UGOD 5112.description: This course introduces how AI and modern computer vision methods can be used to sense, analyze, and understand cities from multi-source data. The course covers an end-to-end pipeline from urban sensing data acquisition and image preprocessing to machine learning, deep learning, 3D reconstruction, generative modeling, and multimodal/foundation models, with a strong focus on practical urban applications and a research-oriented final project.

UGOD 5112.title: Machine Learning in Remote Sensing
UGOD 5112.description: This course focuses on applying machine and deep learning methods for remote sensing and covers a variety of practical applications of remote sensing image processing in complex urban environments. Through a mixture of theoretical and hands-on sessions, students will gain a deeper understanding of advanced image analysis methods and will be able to apply new concepts and approaches to enhance their problem-solving abilities in the interdisciplinary field using multi-source geo-information.

UGOD 5120.title: Entrepreneurship and Modern Economy
UGOD 5120.description: This course studies the role of entrepreneurship in the modern economy. Theories and empirics of startups as a driver of job creation, growth and development, and business cycles will be discussed. The course also examines the effects on venture growth, wealth accumulation, inequality, and innovation in a society. Finally, examples of entrepreneurial public policies will be demonstrated and assessed.
cilos: Understand the theories and empirics of entrepreneurship in relation to the modern economy.
Analyze contemporary public policy issues concerning entrepreneurship and the impact on the society.
Understand and critically assess the literature on entrepreneurship and the modern economy.
Present and communicate recent research on entrepreneurship and the modern economy.
Write an original research paper on entrepreneurship and the modern economy by going through the original research process covered in this course.

UGOD 5130.title: Field Experiments in Social and Policy Research
UGOD 5130.description: The course provides a systematic introduction to field experiments, specifically randomized controlled trials (RCTs) conducted in real-world settings. Students will learn how to design, analyze, and interpret these experiments, understanding their practical significance for applied economics, business, and public policy. The course covers essential statistical principles alongside practical guidelines for conducting fieldwork. We will explore instructive examples across various topics, including urban development, transportation, labor markets, the platform economy, and other relevant policy fields.
cilos: Understand the pros and cons of different methodological approaches to causal inference.
Design a field experiment to answer empirical and theoretical questions.
Implement a field experiment in complex real-world settings, especially those in the Chinese context.
Combine quantitative and qualitative methods.
Understand the threats to inference in the experiment.
Communicate effectively in experimental design and analysis with researchers and practitioners.

UGOD 5140.title: Urban Economics and Policy Analysis
UGOD 5140.description: This course examines the economic forces driving urban development, combining theoretical frameworks with real-world policy challenges. Key topics include agglomeration and systems of cities, urban growth and its spatial forms (sprawl vs. densification), land use patterns (zoning and growth control), transportation (road network, transit, and congestion), housing (affordability, informality, and renewal), and the role of local governments. The course will also highlight recent disruptive forces such as remote work, autonomous vehicles, platform economy, and digital governance in different urban contexts. Through case studies in policy analysis, students will become familiar with classical causal inference research design and learn to leverage emerging data sources, such as AIpowered textual repositories, satellite and street imagery, sensors, GPS, and social media.

UGOD 5150.title: Big Data for Urban Modeling
UGOD 5150.description: This course explores how big data transforms our understanding and modeling of urban systems. Students will develop computational thinking, creative problem framing, and the ability to integrate heterogeneous datasets to address typical urban challenges. Emphasis is placed on data-driven modeling, data thinking, and innovative applications across mobility, health, social sensing, and urban planning.
cilos: Apply computational thinking to frame urban problems computationally.
Critically assess and creatively utilize diverse datasets.
Employ proper methods for urban modelling.
Evaluate ethical, social, and sustainability implications of data-driven urban decision-making.
Design and prototype an innovative urban modelling project using big data.

UGOD 5160.title: Applied Natural Language Processing for Social Inquiry
UGOD 5160.description: This course provides an applied introduction to natural language processing (NLP) techniques for social inquiry, equipping students with the skills to analyze large-scale English and Chinese textual data. Through hands-on labs and real-world case studies, students learn core methods including text preprocessing, dictionary approaches, topic models, embeddings, and supervised classification. Emphasis is placed on methodological applications, interpretation, and the practical use of NLP tools to investigate social, political, cultural, and urban phenomena. Students will also gain exposure to the emerging uses and challenges of large language models (LLMs) in social research, as well as introductory perspectives on applying computational approaches to visual data.
cilos: Explain core natural language processing (NLP) concepts and their relevance for social inquiry.
Perform text preprocessing and representation for large-scale English and Chinese textual data.
Apply key NLP techniques to analyze social, political, cultural, and urban phenomena.
Interpret computational results in theoretically meaningful and practically relevant ways using case studies.
Use large language models (LLMs) and understand their practical applications and limitations in social research.
Recognize how visual data and computer vision approaches can complement textual analysis in applied social inquiry.
Communicate analytical findings effectively through an individual presentation.

UGOD 5200.title: Applied Demography
UGOD 5200.description: This course provides an introduction to applied demography, the practical applications of demographic analysis. Students will learn about the basic principles of demographic analysis, including measures of population size, composition, and distribution, as well as methods for analyzing demographic changes and trends over time. Through hands-on instruction, students will also learn the applications of these techniques to real-world situations, such as policy-making, urban planning, and marketing.

UGOD 5201.title: Spatial Econometrics for Urban Analysis
UGOD 5201.description: This course combines spatial analysis and econometrics to understand and analyze urban phenomena. It equips students with theoretical foundations and practical tools for understanding and analyzing urban data. The course covers spatial autocorrelation, heterogeneity, and various spatial econometric models. It also explores real-world applications in the fields of urban economics, regional science, and environmental economics.

UGOD 5300.title: Introduction to GeoAI
UGOD 5300.description: GeoAI is an interdisciplinary field of Geography/GIScience and Artificial Intelligence (AI), aiming to harness AI techniques to address diverse environmental and societal challenges related to geospatial domain. The course will introduce fundamental concepts, methods, and tools of GeoAI, and show how emerging urban spatio-temporal data and GeoAI technologies can be applied to address urban challenges, improve urban governance and management, and enhance the overall livability and sustainability of cities.

UGOD 5555.title: Urban Simulation with Network Science and Agent-Based Modeling
UGOD 5555.description: This course familiarizes students with modeling urban systems using Network Science and Agent-Based Modeling (ABM). They will design and implement simulations to study urban phenomena such as human dynamics and urban development. Through ABM, students will create computational models of individual agents interacting within urban environments to explore emergent patterns and complex system behaviors. Through Network Science, students will learn to represent urban systems as graphs and apply machine-learning techniques to analyze networks like street layouts and mobility patterns.
cilos: Explain the fundamental concepts of Network Science and Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) as they relate to urban systems.
Design and implement agent-based models using tools like NetLogo to simulate urban phenomena such as human dynamics and urban development.
Apply advanced machine-learning techniques to analyze urban networks and interpret the results.
Analyze simulation outcomes to gain insights into complex urban behaviors and development patterns.
Integrate different technologies into urban simulation to enhance modeling capabilities.
Present modeling processes and findings through academic writings and presentations.

UGOD 5600.title: Qualitative Research with Generative AI
UGOD 5600.description: This course will provide an overview of qualitative and mixed-methods research for human-centered social and technological studies in the digital era. The course will begin with a discussion of major research methodologies and paradigms. We will delve into research design with mainstream qualitative and mixed methods approaches. The course will then introduce specific techniques for collecting, analyzing, integrating, and reporting human-centered data from multiple sources. They include data collection methods such as interviews and focus groups, and data analysis methods such as thematic analysis. Students will engage in utilizing cutting-edge AI tools and techniques to conduct qualitative research. The main goal is to equip students with relevant knowledge, skills, and awareness of using proper methods in solving research questions in social science studies.
cilos: Critically evaluate and compare the use of different approaches to research designs, methods within a specific research area and context.
Understand key paradigmatic debates about mixed-methods research methodology.
Learn major qualitative research approaches and techniques for urban studies.
Understand how to integrate different approaches in a mixed-methods study.
Apply suitable methods for different research questions relating to urban issues.
Interpret and communicate results of qualitative and mixed research.

UGOD 5700.title: Categorical Data Analysis
UGOD 5700.description: This course focuses on statistical analysis of data that are categorical or non-continuous in nature. The contents cover a family of statistical models that deal with binary data, discrete data, count data, and categorical data with special features such as truncation and overdispersion. The course gives emphasis to modeling techniques and hands-on applications to empirical research.

UGOD 6000.title: Independent Study
UGOD 6000.description: Independent study in a designated subject under direct guidance of a faculty member to provide students the advanced knowledge and research skill sets on urban governance and design related topics. Required readings, tutorial discussions, and submission of report(s) will be used for assessment. The course may be repeated for credit if different topics are studied.
cilos: Demonstrate mastery of the knowledge and skills in the selected topics related to Urban Governance and Design.
Apply an interdisciplinary approach in examining the selected topics.
Critically evaluate different aspects of the selected topics.
Communicate findings effectively in written reports.

UGOD 6100.title: Special Topics in Urban Governance and Design
UGOD 6100.description: This course covers emerging topics of Urban Governance and Design concerns not covered in the present curriculum. The course aims to provide students with the advanced knowledge and research skill sets on an Urban Governance and Design topic. Required readings, tutorial discussions, and submission of report(s) will be used for assessment. The course may be repeated for credit if different topics are studied. May be graded by letter or P/F for different offerings.

UGOD 6101.title: UGOD Program Seminar I
UGOD 6101.description: Advanced seminar series presented by postgraduate students, faculty, and guest speakers on selected topics in urban governance and design. This course is offered once a year. Graded P or F.
cilos: Apply essential skills in communicating research results.
Use appropriate software or technologies to deliver an effective presentation.
Communicate effectively in professional settings.
Interact with guest lecturers.

UGOD 6102.title: UGOD Program Seminar II
UGOD 6102.description: Selected topics in hands-on data analyses, such as statistical software (R, STATA, or SAS), data management, and visualization, will be introduced to students in urban governance and design for their research. The course is offered once a year. Graded P or F.
cilos: Apply basic skills in statistical software.
Demonstrate hands-on skills in data management.
Apply fundamental knowledge of integrating data from different sources.
Utilize appropriate tools to visualize the data.
Apply the skills to a project on data analysis with application to UGOD topics in the real world.

UGOD 6990.title: MPhil Thesis Research
UGOD 6990.description: Master's thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.
cilos: Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in Urban Governance & Design.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.

UGOD 7990.title: Doctoral Thesis Research
UGOD 7990.description: Original and independent doctoral thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.
cilos: Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in Urban Governance & Design.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.
